clue.text: Loose liver's heading into wonderful times

indicators.note: into tells us the letter goes inside the word for wonderful

parts.note: fab is slang for fabulous or wonderful

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of liver's is used

parts.note: by means times, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Someone's liver gets a mention as the drinker heads into good times.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby flesh is slack and soft, so loose is a fair synonym here.

indicators.note: carrying means the coachman holds the artist inside

parts.note: William Fargo founded Wells Fargo, the old American stagecoach company
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A stagecoach driver of old takes a painter aboard amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells Fargo was the American stagecoach firm, which is why the coachman is old.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or mixture, much like a shambles.

indicators.note: accessing means the leader is found getting into the word Lakelands

explanation.surface: A Scout leader is getting into the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela, from Kipling's Jungle Book wolf, is the title of a Cub Scout pack leader.

explanation.surface: A note on a fortified drink from a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital and chief port of Oman, and also a sweet wine made from muscat grapes.

explanation.surface: Something rough is, logically, strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven ground is bumpy; and a number that is not even is, by that token, odd.

indicators.note: in places the hair inside the actor's surname

parts.note: Montgomery Clift was a Hollywood actor
locks are hair

explanation.surface: A mountain conveyance has its tresses in a general's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Montgomery' suggests the wartime British general, but here it is the Hollywood actor Montgomery Clift.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairlift carries skiers up the slopes, a typical Alpine conveyance.

clue.text: Once you've seen one shopping centre, you've seen Buckingham Palace's approach

definitions.text: Once you've seen one shopping centre, you've seen Buckingham Palace's approach

parts.words: Once you've seen one shopping centre, you've seen Buckingham Palace's approach
parts.note: the saying 'once you've seen one, you've seen ...' is bent so its final words, rerun, make a shopping centre that is also the avenue up to the royal residence

explanation.surface: A jaded tourist finds all malls alike, and London's royal avenue no different.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mall is the ceremonial road leading to Buckingham Palace in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mall is the ceremonial avenue leading up to Buckingham Palace, and a mall is a shopping centre.

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests the letters are elaborately rearranged

explanation.surface: A punter wonders whether the bookie's tipster likes the odds offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' signals an anagram; the whole clue also describes the tipster, who fancies a horse and its starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tipster recommends horses to back, so he might well fancy a price.

clue.text: Step with scoundrel into group, person distanced from reality

indicators.note: into shows the first pieces go inside the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group of things
a pace is a step
a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue steps into a crowd, while someone daydreams far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A space cadet is an idiom for a dreamy, absent-minded person out of touch with reality.

clue.text: A fool needs little time to open beer, perhaps, as source of food

indicators.note: to open means the inner pieces split the reworked beer apart
perhaps suggests the letters of beer might be arranged some other way

parts.note: nana is British slang for a silly person
t is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An idiot spends a moment cracking open a beer, maybe while looking for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' could be the dessert, but here it is slang for a silly person; 'perhaps' shuffles beer before the pieces open it.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical plant bears the familiar curved yellow fruit, so it is a provider of food.

clue.text: I yell as you hear a child's demand?

indicators.note: as you hear signals that the phrase is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to yell is to scream, so I yell gives I scream

explanation.surface: Someone shouts like a toddler wanting a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: From the rhyme 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert is the classic treat small children beg for, hence a child's demand.

clue.text: Breakfast food made greasy, filling tramp after release of gas

indicators.note: filling means one piece is packed inside the other
after release of means the gas letters are let out of the word for tramp

parts.note: a beggar is a tramp
Ar is the chemical symbol for argon, a gas
oiled means made greasy

explanation.surface: A dish turned oily stuffs a vagrant who has just broken wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Ar is argon, so 'release of gas' is a schoolboy joke hiding a chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked in its shell in water is a standard breakfast dish.

clue.text: Descend down, as representative of Cambridge

parts.note: to light, as in alight, is to descend and settle
blue means down or sad

explanation.surface: Coming down glumly, as a Cambridge delegate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Light Blue is a sportsperson chosen to represent Cambridge University, whose colour is light blue.

parts.note: to sag is to drop or droop

explanation.surface: A request to put down a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally a Norse heroic tale.

clue.text: Winter sportsman's assistant finds swimmer grabbing forty winks

indicators.note: grabbing means the fish takes hold of the nap within itself

parts.note: a sole is a fish, so a swimmer
a kip is a short sleep, forty winks

explanation.surface: A skier's aid is a fish snatching a quick nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a person, but it is a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski pole helps a skier balance and push off, an aid to a winter sportsman.

indicators.note: something controversial is disputed and unsettled, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that something shows the Scientology founder's ideas are disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dianetics is the system of ideas devised by L Ron Hubbard, the basis of Scientology.

clue.text: Formal requirement to kiss, given relationship

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
a tie is a bond or relationship

explanation.surface: Kissing is required for a formal relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a standard item of formal dress, often required by dress codes.

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A clipped cigarette stub.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short.

clue.text: Take action about rubbish work of art

indicators.note: about means the legal action goes around the rubbish

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone goes to court over a worthless piece of artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a work of art.

annotationWithheld.why: 'T' indicates 'Talks in the office' (8): the only parse splits 'indicates' into the container word 'in' and the fodder 'dicates', one clue word doing two jobs, which the grammar cannot record

indicators.note: in places the male pronoun inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the core is the middle of something
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: An instruction to glue a figure at the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together as a whole.

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of born thursday run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone born midweek is an untamed creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' signals an anagram of BORN THURSDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: This bustard is a type of large ground-dwelling bird.

clue.text: Poet backing bad taste, though men refuse to put it down

definitions.text: though men refuse to put it down

indicators.note: backing means the poet's name is read from the end

parts.note: T S Eliot is the poet

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of taste have gone wrong and need reordering

explanation.surface: A versifier supports vulgarity, while men stubbornly leave something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ELIOT into TOILE; 'bad' rearranges TASTE to TSEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Men are notoriously accused of leaving the lavatory seat raised instead of lowering it.

clue.text: A kid struggling during run, as animals flat out

indicators.note: during means the scrambled letters sit within the word for run

parts.note: roll can mean run, as cameras or presses roll

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of a kid are thrashing about out of order

explanation.surface: A young goat fights while running, and creatures end up lying flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' scrambles the goat and its article; 'during' sets them after the first two letters of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadkill is animals hit by traffic and left lying squashed on the road.

clue.text: Hole some clientele yet to reject

indicators.note: to reject means the extracted run is thrown back and read in the other direction
some means only part of the letters of clientele yet are taken

explanation.surface: A gap that some customers are still to turn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes TELEYE from clienTELE YEt, and 'to reject' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced hole for a lace or cord to pass through.

clue.text: Setter not quite accepting state as Doctor of Literature

indicators.note: accepting means the shortened word takes the state's letters inside it
not quite drops the final letter of the word for setter

parts.note: jelly is a substance that sets
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky, a US state

explanation.surface: The puzzle's compiler, not fully committed, takes on a role as a literary physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is something that sets in the fridge; 'not quite' trims its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Jekyll is the doctor of Stevenson's novella, a doctor found in literature.
